question: Who among the following was one of the recipients of the Nobel Prize in Physics 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Syukuro Manabe**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Syukuro Manabe is a Japanese-American climatologist who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2021.
 
• He received the Nobel Prize for his work on the physical modeling of Earth's climate, quantifying variability, and predicting global warming.
 
• Manabe's research in the 1960s demonstrated how increased levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere would lead to higher temperatures at the Earth's surface.
 
• His pioneering work has been foundational in the field of climate science, contributing significantly to our understanding of climate change and its impacts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nobel Prize**

 
 
• The Nobel Prizes are international awards given annually in several categories such as Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, and Peace.
 
• Established by the 1895 will of Alfred Nobel, the prizes are awarded to individuals or organizations that have made significant contributions to humanity.
 
• The Nobel Prize in Physics is awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.
 
 
 
• **Climate Models**
 
 
• Climate models are mathematical representations of the climate system based on physical principles governing the atmosphere, oceans, and land surface.
 
• These models are used to simulate the interactions of the atmosphere, oceans, land surface, and ice.
 
• They help in predicting future climate changes by taking into account various factors like greenhouse gas emissions, solar radiation, and other climatic variables.
 
 
 
• **Global Warming**
 
 
• Global warming refers to the long-term rise in the average temperature of the Earth's climate system.
 
• It is primarily caused by the increase in greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane due to human activities like burning fossil fuels and deforestation.
 
• Global warming has significant impacts on the environment, including rising sea levels, extreme weather events, and loss of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Gases**
 
 
• Greenhouse gases are gases that trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere, leading to the greenhouse effect.
 
• Major greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, and fluorinated gases.
 
• Human activities such as burning fossil fuels, industrial processes, and agricultural practices have significantly increased the concentration of these gases in the atmosphere.
